usage: The standard question when meeting someone, here in the form addressed to a man. The ending changes with who you are asking: ismuka to a man, ismuki to a woman. It is neutral in tone; with an older person or in a formal setting the polite form with al-karim is better.

variants.label: to a group
variants.note: Use when asking several people at once.

variants.label: very polite
variants.note: Use with elders, clients, or anyone you want to show respect.

variants.label: blunt
variants.note: Asks who someone is rather than their name; can sound abrupt.

responses.english: My name is Ahmad, and you?

examples.english: Excuse me, what is your name, miss?
What is your name and where are you from?
